reflexion_entries_to_archive: S170 P1: #a-black-sheet-cannot-express-two-visibility-rules: S166, S169 and my own first attempt each tried to fix 'backdrop visible AND buildings hidden' by MOVING the backdrop, and all three failed, because with an opaque full-canvas sheet the requirement is not expressible by ordering at all - anything visible must be above the sheet, and anything above it paints over everything below. Three sessions of relocation were spent on a constraint nobody had stated. LESSON: when two placements of one object both produce bugs, stop moving it and write down the invariant; if the invariant is contradictory, the MECHANISM is wrong, not the position. The fix was to move concealment off the canvas and onto the objects (an inverse mask), after which the backdrop needed no special position at all.

S170 P2: #a-green-test-can-be-defending-the-bug: the owner reported the same two-pharaoh defect twice and S169 'fixed' it by removing the gate that was PROVABLE in a unit test (a direct-dispatch latch) while leaving the gate he actually hit. t9BossTower.test.ts asserted the waiting behaviour as CORRECT, so the suite was green ON the defect and would have blocked the real fix. LESSON: when a reported bug 'does not reproduce' in tests but the owner keeps reporting it, grep for a test that ASSERTS the reported behaviour - a defect with a passing test defending it is invisible to every gate. Also: the docblock defending that gate justified itself by citing the latch S169 had just deleted, so a stale rationale outlived its own premise.

S170 P2b: #gate-the-effect-on-the-outcome-not-on-the-trigger: the drone's blast VFX was pushed unconditionally, BEFORE the enemy-only candidate scan and the owner-sparing damage - so a fuse-expiry detonation at home showed a full shock ring for an event that could not damage anything. The tempting fix (silence blasts on fuse expiry) would have silenced real hits too, since explode-in-place next to an enemy base is deliberate. LESSON: gate a visual on what actually HAPPENED (candidates.length), never on the branch that led there.

S170 P3: #one-populations-ceiling-silently-gating-another: GOBLIN_MAX_PER_SPAWNER=10 was shared by the goblin tower and the tier-3 race towers, so a tier-3 tower went permanently silent at ten units - the owner's original 'the Piranha didn't produce at all' returning, months later, from a constant named after a different unit. Three prior exclusions in the same function existed for exactly this failure and a fourth was still owed. LESSON: fix it as an EXEMPTION, never by raising or deleting the shared number, and assert BOTH sides - a test proving 'tier 3 is uncapped' cannot tell that from 'the cap is gone' and would have re-tuned an economy the owner chose.

S170 P4: #the-unit-of-a-ruling-is-part-of-the-ruling: the sudoku trial counted SHAPES with an exact test; the owner had said 'twelve same-shape-connectors' and the code's own comment flagged that one word would flip it - and nobody asked him for two sessions while he reported 'there is no sudoku, it doesn't work'. Twelve connectors is not a fixed shape count (chain of 13 = ring of 12 = 12 bonds), so no shape-count test could express his rule. LESSON: when a comment says 'one word flips this if the intent was X', that is an OWNER QUESTION, not a note. And an exact-N test on a value that can jump by two is skippable by construction.

S170 P5: #a-private-renderer-method-scopes-a-condition-to-one-renderer: the stun stars lived as a private method of goblinRenderer, which silently limited them to GOBLIN_KINDS - while applyStun's only caller, the Kraken sonar, has NO type filter and stuns voltkin/chewer/drones drawn by two other renderers. Those froze with no stars, reading as a hang. The same method also used flat geometry, so on the scaled-up bosses (the units stun exists to counter) the ring sat inside the sprite. LESSON: a visual for a property of an ENTITY belongs in a module, not in whichever renderer happened to add it. Extraction is also what made it testable - it went from an untestable private method to a pure function with a determinism assertion.
